messages:
Mike P: Hi team — kicking off a PRD intake for routing improvements for latency-sensitive requests. Problem: some customers (esp. streaming/chat) see spike tail latencies when requests route to higher-cost model variants. We need a clear MVP and success metrics to prioritize this on the roadmap.

Mike P: Problem statement: routing currently prioritizes model quality then cost, which causes occasional 99.9p latency regressions under bursty traffic. Customer impact: poor UX for live chat, missed SLAs for Dedicated customers.

Mike P: Goals: (1) Define a routing policy framework that allows per-route latency SLOs; (2) Implement a low-risk MVP that enforces a latency-first route (fallback to quality when safe); (3) Clear rollout and metrics for regression detection.

Mike P: Non-goals: re-architecting the scheduler or changing kernel selection logic; deep model retraining.

Mike P: Success metrics: 99p latency reduction for routing-sensitive routes by >=30% within first week of rollout; no more than 0.5% increase in token-cost for those routes; zero customer-facing errors during rollout.

Sara G: A couple q's: how strict are the latency SLOs? e.g., 99p under 200ms or 500ms? Also do we want per-customer overrides?

Mike P: Good q — propose defaults: 99p <= 300ms for chat streaming. Allow per-customer override via route config (opt-in). For Dedicated tenants we expose toggle in Console.

Andrew L: For MVP I suggest a flags-based approach: routing policy field on route config e.g. `latency_priority: high|normal|cost` and a fallback chain. Minimal change to runtime. Example config: 
```
route: chat-stream
latency_priority: high
latency_slo_ms: 300
fallback_chain: [low-latency-variant, standard-variant]
```
Will need metrics hook for per-request chosen_variant and latency buckets.

Jessica H: UI note: Console needs an affordance to set latency_priority and show historical 99/95/50p. Short term: add field to route edit modal + small tooltip. Long term: chart on route dashboard.

Oliver C: Customer context — Acme Health reported chat lag during peak hours. They need determinism rather than slightly better quality. They'll accept a small cost bump. They asked for per-route toggle and audit logs.

Sara G: Engineering questions: (1) How do we detect when quality fallback is needed? Do we sample outputs and run evals? (2) Rollback: auto-fallback if quality drop > X% on evals?

Mike P: Answer: initial approach — no automatic quality-detect fallback. Fallbacks are policy-ordered variants; quality regression monitoring via periodic evals on a small prompt set (daily sampling). Alert if quality drops >5% vs baseline, then manual rollback/adjustment.

Andrew L: Implementation plan (MVP): 1) Add policy field on route config (API + Console), 2) Router reads field and prefers variants with known latency profiles, 3) Emit metrics (chosen_variant, latency_ms, cost_tokens) to Console + Prom. Est time: 3 sprints to get end-to-end (1 sprint for API/console toggle + 2 for router + metrics + canary).

Jessica H: For canary UX we should allow per-route canary percent and show side-by-side latency/cost. I can mock quick screens next week.

Oliver C: I'll surface to Acme Health and verify they can test a canary. They want a canary on Dedicated non-prod pool first.

Mike P: Acceptance criteria (draft): 
- Route config API accepts latency_priority and latency_slo_ms fields.
- Router respects priority and picks variant that keeps expected p99 within SLO for normal load.
- Metrics emitted: route, chosen_variant, latency_ms histogram, token_cost.
- Console UI to toggle latency_priority and show p99 chart.
- Canary rollout plan documented with rollback steps and alert thresholds.

Mike P: Edge cases to consider: cold-start variance on new variants, multi-model sessions (context must pin), autoscaling spikes. Note these in PRD.

Sara G: Sounds reasonable. One follow-up: need definition of "expected p99" — is it historical moving window (30m) or model-profiled? prefer combination: model-profile baseline + 30m sliding.

Mike P: Agreed — add as acceptance detail.

Andrew L: I'll draft an RFC with APIs and router pseudocode. Will include sample policy YAML and metrics schema.

Jessica H: I'll add sketches and a content short explaining tradeoffs (latency vs cost).

Oliver C: I'll coordinate customer validation.

deploy-bot: Note: /link to open RFC draft: https://rfd.internal/redwood/routing-latency-priority (draft)

Mike P: Thanks all — assigning owners: Andrew = eng lead, Sara = eng support, Jessica = design, Oliver = CS validation. Adding to roadmap discussion next Thurs. If anyone objects to the MVP scope speak now, otherwise I'll convert to PRD template and add acceptance items. :thumbsup:

Sara G: :thumbsup:

Jessica H: :+1:

Oliver C: Will follow up with customer timeline.
